the balk is a beat (the fairness pass): the Walker is set afoot leading the horse through the water, and back on dry ground it picks them up again

the mounted law (the fairness pass): a runner who sees the gap growing under hooves gives up the chase, so a horse at speed is not caught; a knife's blow landed on a Walker standing in the saddle still bolts it, and it trots back when the trouble is done
